I want to share my personal experience with HSNC University, Mumbai. My daughter was struggling to get admission, and we had almost lost hope. At the last moment, when I decided to visit the college one more time, we met Miss Rekha — the person who truly changed everything for us.

Today, my daughter is very happy in this college. She loves attending her classes and feels comfortable and motivated every day. The atmosphere, the staff, and the overall environment are truly excellent.
The infrastructure is also very impressive — spacious, modern, and well maintained.

I also want to mention the cleanliness and hygiene of the campus. The washrooms are exceptionally clean, honestly 5-star rated. The canteen is amazing — clean, hygienic, and serves good quality food. Even the watchmen are very kind and honest, always ready to help and guide students and parents.

A heartfelt thanks to the entire college team, and a special thanks to Miss Rekha for being such a wonderful and supportive person. We are truly grateful.

I enrolled in The WorldGrad after being influenced by representations regarding overseas education outcomes, including claims such as a “2X higher visa success rate” and alumni success examples displayed on their platform.

Over time, I became concerned about the actual outcomes being experienced by students in my cohort, particularly regarding visa results and the gap between marketing representations and what I observed in reality. These concerns significantly affected my confidence in continuing with the program.

I raised these concerns directly with the company, along with personal circumstances affecting my ability to proceed. Initially, no refund was offered, but a partial refund of ₹3 lakh was later provided after discussions.

Since my matter remains unsolved I have  filed consumer grievances and an ASCI complaint requesting review of the advertising claims and representations involved.

I would strongly encourage prospective students to independently verify visa outcomes, university pathways, refund policies, and marketing claims before making a substantial financial commitment.

Thank you for your response!
Since I cannot reply you I am adding my response to your reply here.

My concerns were not limited to personal circumstances. Prior to the partial refund, I had also raised concerns directly regarding the credibility of the program, marketing representations, and the outcomes being experienced by students.

While I understand that no explicit visa guarantee may have been provided, claims such as “2X higher visa success rate” and alumni outcome representations significantly influenced my enrollment decision and expectations regarding overseas study progression.

Regarding payment, I paid approximately ₹8.55 lakhs toward the stages of the program I completed. I did not proceed with paying for the remaining stages after developing serious concerns regarding the outcomes being experienced and the overall credibility of the representations made.

I have also raised these concerns through official consumer grievance channels, where multiple reminders have reportedly been sent without response from the company.

The matter has therefore been escalated through appropriate consumer and advertising complaint channels for independent review.

featured_reviews.review_text:
As a student navigating the corridors of Mumbai University, I am compelled to share a deeply disappointing experience that reflects systemic neglect and administrative apathy.
Despite being one of the largest universities in India, the management here operates with alarming inefficiency. Students are routinely subjected to long queues, unresolved grievances, and a complete lack of accountability. The grievance redressal mechanism is virtually non-existent—when asked about it, staff either deny its existence or redirect students to the Board of Examinations, which itself remains inaccessible and unresponsive.
Staff members are frequently "on lunch break" or "in meetings," and when available, their tone is often dismissive or outright rude. Doors are shut during working hours while students wait outside, seeking basic assistance. Emails sent to official departments go unanswered, and technical issues plague even the simplest processes—from mark sheets to exam forms.
The quality of education, sadly, mirrors this dysfunction. There is little regard for student welfare, dignity, or timely resolution. The culture seems to prioritize internal comfort over public service, with staff enjoying leisurely breaks funded by student fees, while students struggle for clarity and support.
Mumbai University must urgently introspect and reform. Students deserve respect, transparency, and a functioning system—not bureaucratic indifference masked as procedure

featured_reviews.name: Charvi Dedhia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hansraj Jivandas College of Education is truly one of the finest institutions for anyone who dreams of becoming a professional, confident, and compassionate teacher. My experience here has been nothing short of transformative. The college doesn’t just teach you how to teach it grooms you into an educator who can multitask, manage responsibilities, and carry yourself with professionalism and grace.

The faculty is absolutely fabulous. Every teacher is well-trained, supportive, and genuinely invested in our growth. They don’t just deliver lessons; they mentor, guide, and push us to bring out the best version of ourselves. Whether it’s Usha Borkar ma’am, Pallavi Talekar ma’am, Archana Katgeri ma’am, Karuna Sinha ma’am, Shrima Bannerjee ma’am or Vaishali Sawant ma’am, or any other member of the teaching and support staff each one of them contributes immensely to a warm, encouraging, and enriching learning environment.

The college atmosphere is fun, loving, and full of positivity. The internship journey, though challenging, is like a roller-coaster ride that teaches you real classroom skills, patience, adaptability, and the true essence of being a teacher. You come out of it stronger, sharper, and more confident.

A special mention must be made of our Principal, Dr. Geeta Shetty. She is the heart of the institution warm, kind, approachable, and inspiring. Her guidance feels like gold, and she leads the college with a beautiful balance of discipline and empathy.

If you are planning to pursue a B.Ed, I can wholeheartedly say that Hansraj Jivandas College of Education is the best choice you can make. It not only shapes you into a skilled educator but also into a better person. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Namrata Nayar
featured_reviews.review_text:
What should have been a review has become a eulogy, as I was just informed that Dr. Sampat is no more.

A great principal isn’t just a leader; they are a force. They shape minds, build character, and leave a mark so deep that even years later, their words echo in your heart.

Dr. Urmi Sampat was that kind of principal. She wasn’t just an educator,she was an institution.

I still remember my first day at H.J. College. She stood at the gate in a crisp cream saree, radiating authority yet warmth. “What’s your name?” she asked. “Namrata  , and I’m am going to be the topper this year,” I replied with pride. She just laughed and said, “Go and sit yourself inside.” That was Dr. Sampat, no fuss, no unnecessary praise, just straight to the point. But in that moment, she acknowledged me. And with her, an acknowledgment always meant something.

She had this aura about her,if she caught you in the corridor, you’d hold your breath. If you were exhaling, you wouldn’t dare inhale again until she passed. That was the kind of presence she had. But beneath that formidable exterior was someone who truly believed in her students.

I remember struggling in my psychology paper. She called me in and asked, “What the hell have you done?” I admitted, “I had a blackout.” She didn’t let me off easily. “I don’t believe in blackouts, but I believe in you,” she said. And that belief changed me. I promised her I wouldn’t let her down. And when I topped my methods, she awarded me the prestigious Miss H.J Title of the year. That moment shaped my future in ways I didn’t even realise at the time.

One of the greatest compliments I’ve ever received came from her:

Personally, I see a junior Dr. Urmi Sampat in Namrata.
That comparison still humbles me.

Everything she taught me stayed with me. From my first lesson at NPKT to my journey as a teacher at Arya Vidya Mandir Bandra, to moving to Dubai , her words have never left me. The discipline, the passion, the high standards,they are woven into the way I lead today.

I wish I had the chance to say goodbye. But in a way, someone like her never truly leaves. Somewhere, I know she’s making sure everyone arrives on time, does their job well, and carries themselves with the grace and dignity she expected of us all.

Dr. Sampat, you were the epitome of grace, excellence, and discipline. They don’t make them like you anymore. I treasured you, and I always will.
Yours truly,
Namrata Simon Nayar

featured_reviews.name: Shami Sayed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Avoid.

I studied B.Ed. here and it was a traumatic experience for me. I couldn't find a detail review about this place, so I will present a honest review.

Although the quality of teacher education in most institutes is pathetic, this is a terrible place to be in if one wants to become a good teacher. If you want to be a teacher who has empathy and kindness for children then this isn't a good place because you might be pushed to be otherwise.

Some points to keep in mind before taking admission here:
1. Most "teachers" are openly partial and discriminating. They get a FAT salary by the government and "train" those students who on average will get a paltry sum of salary and this perhaps give them a sense of excessive superiority. They are miserly tyrants as they will demand you to get their personal and unrelated errands (mazdoori) done for free. Don't know if the old principal who was unreachable to students except till the last day also treated them like that, but their nervousness infront of her betrayed a sign of incompetence.

2. In the name of discipline you will get to be treated as a slave. True discipline is about following the rules which is good but these people are not concerned about rules and openly flout it e.g. wrongly confining the original documents, forcing students to do things that they are not required to according to the actual curriculum they paid the fees for, and some of them won't bat an eye to give mean degrading remarks. They forget that there's a Constitution which has certain rules for state-funded institutes.

3. The NAAC grade is a joke which they got by accommodating the officers in an expensive Juhu hotel (as proudly but ignorantly revealed by one "teacher")

4. The senior clerk Aditi Nerurkar is a hateful mean bigot (and possibly a psychopath) who seems to have been given a free hand by the college to be as such.

5. Teaching skills before joining this course won't be much different after completing it, and of course it will be because what can you learn when people (most teachers) who don't have subject content knowledge nor could they understand education in so many years, lectures you for hours 6 days a week and makes you study from poor content ripped off online. But you can become a drama artist (or dancer) because that's what happens often on priority.

6. Internships are held like the horrible show of big boss contest without any checks and balances for how students behave towards each other, but it's of not much concern to them of course because it doesn't affect them. It's majorly a total waste of time and you'll get the same repetitive feedback so basically you aren't growing as a teacher.

The only "strong point" of this course is the class presentation / speech which is simply about blabbering stuffs. Sadly, there isn't any good that I find here except maybe punctuality and obediance? Not sure if this place has always been like that since 1969, if so then I can't imagine their contribution to society. Either way, I don't know why they always demand to be worshipped.

featured_reviews.name: Musafir Hun Yaaron
featured_reviews.review_text:
The University of Mumbai, established in 1857, is one of India’s oldest and most prestigious institutions. It offers a diverse range of undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs across disciplines such as science, commerce, arts, management, engineering, law, and social sciences.  ￼ ￼

The university operates primarily from two campuses: the Fort Campus, known for its historic Rajabai Clock Tower, and the expansive Kalina Campus, which spans 243 acres and provides a serene environment conducive to learning and research.  ￼

Students have access to comprehensive facilities, including separate hostels for boys and girls, well-furnished rooms, spacious classrooms, and full-time internet connectivity.  The Jawaharlal Nehru Library serves as a central resource, housing an extensive collection of academic materials.  ￼ ￼

The university has produced notable alumni who have significantly contributed to various fields. However, some students have expressed concerns regarding placement opportunities, citing limited campus recruitment and lower salary packages.  Despite these challenges, the University of Mumbai remains a prominent educational institution, blending historical significance with academic diversity. ￼
